tools.name: getRelatedRecords
tools.title: Get Related Records
tools.description:
Retrieves child records related to a parent record by traversing relationships.
Use this instead of a separate SOQL query when you already have a record ID and need its related records (e.g., get all Contacts for an Account, or all Opportunity Line Items for an Opportunity).
Supports multi-level traversal (Account → Contacts → Cases).
More efficient than multiple queries when navigating object relationships.
Requires: parent object name, parent record ID, and relationship name (e.g., "Contacts", "Opportunities").

relationship-path.description: Relationship path (supports multiple levels, e.g., 'Account/Owner'). See: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_rest.meta/api_rest/dome_relationship_traversal.htm

tools.name: listRecentSobjectRecords
tools.title: Get Recently Viewed Records
tools.description:
Returns records of a specific type that the user recently viewed or modified.
Use this as a starting point when the user refers to "my accounts," "recent cases," or "that opportunity I was looking at" without providing specific record IDs or names.
Returns up to 2,000 records ordered by last viewed date.
Requires the object API name (e.g., "Account", "Case", "Opportunity").

tools.name: soqlQuery
tools.title: Query Records (SOQL)
tools.description:
Executes a SOQL query to retrieve Salesforce records.
Use this when you know which object and fields you need—it's the primary way to read data.
SOQL syntax: `SELECT fields FROM Object WHERE conditions ORDER BY field LIMIT n`.
Supports relationship queries to traverse lookups (e.g., `Contact.Account.Name`) and subqueries for child records (e.g., `(SELECT Id FROM Contacts)`).
Always include a WHERE clause to filter results and a LIMIT clause to control result size.
For large objects, filter on indexed fields (Id, Name, foreign keys, External IDs) to avoid timeout errors.
Maximum 50,000 total records per transaction across all queries. Example: `SELECT Id, Name, Industry FROM Account WHERE Industry = 'Technology' LIMIT 100`

**When to use SOQL vs SOSL**: Use SOQL when you know which object contains your data and need precise filtering, sorting, aggregation, or relationship traversal. SOQL supports complex WHERE clauses, JOINs via relationships, GROUP BY, and ORDER BY.

tools.name: find
tools.title: Search Across Objects (SOSL)
tools.description:
Executes a text search across multiple objects simultaneously.
Use this instead of `soql_query` when: (1) searching for a term that could exist in multiple object types, (2) you don't know which object contains the data, or (3) you need relevance-ranked text matching.
Returns a maximum of 2,000 records total—if you need more results, use SOQL instead.
Use search groups to narrow scope: `IN ALL FIELDS` (default), `IN NAME FIELDS`, `IN EMAIL FIELDS`, or `IN PHONE FIELDS`. Example: `FIND {Acme} IN NAME FIELDS RETURNING Account(Id, Name), Contact(Id, Name, Email), Opportunity(Id, Name)`

**When to use SOSL vs SOQL**: Use SOSL for "find me anything matching X" scenarios. It cannot traverse relationships or sort results by field values—if you need related records after finding matches, follow up with a SOQL query using the returned IDs. Limited to 20 SOSL queries per transaction (vs. 100 for SOQL).

q.description:
The SOSL query string.

**Examples:**
- FIND {"Joe Smith"}
- FIND {415901} IN Phone FIELDS RETURNING Contact(Id, Phone, FirstName, LastName), Lead(Id, Phone, FirstName, LastName)
- FIND {"Acme*"} IN Name FIELDS RETURNING Account(Id, Name), Opportunity(Id, Name)
- FIND {"*"} IN ALL FIELDS RETURNING Account(Id, Name)

tools.name: getUserInfo
tools.title: Get Current User Info
tools.description:
Returns current user's identity, role, and preferences.
Call this when you need to personalize responses, understand the user's team context, or apply their preferred defaults for currency, date ranges, or report formatting.
Returns: User ID, name, role, profile, manager, local time, timezone, and user-specific preferences configured by admins (e.g., "When showing pipeline, always break out by AE").

tools.name: getObjectSchema
tools.title: Get Object Schema (Enhanced)
tools.description:
Returns Salesforce schema information optimized for LLM consumption.
Call with NO PARAMETERS first to get an index of all queryable objects—this helps you understand what data exists (80-90% smaller than raw describe).
Then call with a specific OBJECT_NAME to get field-level details when you need to construct queries or understand a specific object's structure.
Includes admin-authored guidance about data quality and business definitions (e.g., "use Calculated_ACV__c instead of Amount for accurate forecasting)";

objects.description: Comma-separated object API names (e.g., "Account,Opportunity"). If omitted, returns an index of all objects.
